── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: none recorded.
This week: 6.8 km over 3 runs.
Body: "Calves tight the day after each run, gone by the next morning."
Feeling: "Proud I started."
Asks: "I want to be ready for the 5K in November. Should I run every day next week to get there faster?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: Keep the same three run days and grow each one by a minute or two, with full rest days between. …
Answers: No, please do not run every day next week. You would get there slower, not faster, because new runners' bones, tendons and calves need the off days to adapt, and that is where injuries creep in.
Next week:
Mon: easy, walk-run 22 min (about 2.3 km), same 1 min run / 1 min walk pattern, easy…
Tue: rest, dog walk is fine. Lets the calves recover before Wednesday.
Wed: easy, walk-run 22 min (about 2.3 km), same pattern, flat route. Keeps the mid-week…
Thu: rest, dog walk is fine. Protects Saturday's slightly longer session.
Fri: rest or an easy 20 – 30 min walk. Keeps you loose without adding running load.
Sat: easy, walk-run 26 min (about 2.8 km), same pattern, easy effort. Your longest of…
Sun: rest. Full recovery day before the new week.
